title: Flight Deck: compact observability snapshot pack for onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact, copy-ready snapshot pack ("Flight Deck") of observability dashboards for the onboarding/quickstart flow. The pack will include screenshot-ready panels and annotated callouts for: multi-tenant cost attribution (cost per token by route + customer), per-route p95 latency heatmap, and a distributed trace waterfall with KV cache hit-rate overlay. These assets will be used in the quickstart guide, in-product onboarding modals, and marketing docs to demonstrate how Redwood surfaces latency and cost trade-offs in production.
acceptance_criteria: Three high-resolution PNG panels are produced: cost attribution, latency heatmap, trace waterfall with KV hits overlay
Each panel has a short export-friendly caption (1-2 sentences) and a 2-line tooltip sample for in-product microcopy
Annotations call out the three main levers: batching, KV cache effectiveness, and model variant fallbacks
Assets are available in both light and dark theme variants and sized for 1200x630 (social), 1440x900 (doc hero), and 640x360 (slide)
Design review completed and sign-off from PM and Eng with at most one round of minor visual tweaks
Figma files and a minimal handoff checklist (file names, export sizes, recommended alt text) are uploaded to the Observability Onboarding Confluence page
mockup_notes: Avoid duplicating existing observability screenshots—this pack focuses on compact, narrative-driven panels with callouts for root cause and action paths (e.g., reroute to cheaper model variant, enable KV caching for specific prompt families). Use synthetic but realistic numbers: p95 latency range 120-480ms, cost per token comparisons with highlighted outliers, KV cache hit rates as percent overlays on traces.
accessibility_considerations: Ensure contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for primary data text
Provide alt text for each exported image (included in handoff checklist)
Do not rely solely on color for status—use icons and patterns for heatmap intensity

design_decisions: Use a compact 3-panel hero to communicate single-screen clarity for new users
Prefer annotated callouts tied to actions (e.g., 'Enable KV cache for prompt family X') rather than raw metric dumps
Include both dark and light variants because onboarding appears in customers' consoles and marketing pages
Synthetic telemetry values are realistic but anonymized to avoid customer data leakage
